items.q: What does he mean by the frozen part of the reasoning?
items.a: The language model. You rent the weights. They almost never change. An agent is that model plus a harness, and the harness is what you can make repeatable.

items.q: Why does the room shout worktrees?
items.a: Files have no transactions. Parallel agents each get a copy, then merge to main. That isolates the write. It does not commit it atomically. His hybrid keeps the to-do in a file and promotes a preference into a database.

items.q: What is on the context card?
items.a: Topics, a summary of current intent, facts and preferences, the question still open, and the recent turns. The harness builds it. The weights do not.
The institutional terms colleagues never say out loud. If that page is missing, the model answers through a lens that does not include the company.

items.q: How does a good session become a skill?
items.a: Store it, distill a better skill.md, retire the old file. A library's look or a preferred database can ride along. He gives no test that the new skill is better.

items.q: How much patience does this workshop's model get?
items.a: Eight to twelve tool calls on Grok 4.1 fast, then stop. Hard problems route to a frontier model. Easy ones can take a small open-weight model. Better tool blurbs separate lookalikes. They do not grant access to confidential tables.
